# Options {#sec-options}

Options are set on an environment, and every model made on it reads them. biyos checks each value as it is set and refuses one outside the option's range. [Options](#sec-option-table) lists every option with its default and range.

## Names, ids and kinds {#sec-options-kinds}

An option has a name, such as `maxtime`, and an id, such as `BIYOS_OPT_MAXTIME`. `BIYOS_getoptid` finds the id of a name, so a program can set options it reads from a file.

The kind of an option decides which call sets it: `BIYOS_setenvdblopt` for a double, `BIYOS_setenvintopt` for an int or an enum, and so on ([Options in the C API](#sec-capi-options)). Nothing is converted, so an int option refuses `BIYOS_setenvdblopt`. The values of an enum option are macros, such as `BIYOS_CHK_FULL` for `checking`.

## Setting and reading {#sec-options-set}

This code sets a double option, a bool option, and an enum option found by name:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/options.c" item="set_options"}
```

A refused value leaves the option as it was, and the call returns `BIYOS_ERR_BADARG` with a message saying why ([Errors](#sec-errors)). Reading takes the same ids:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/options.c" item="read_options"}
```

## Two levels {#sec-options-levels}

A model may hold its own value of an option, which it reads before the environment's. Each call on the environment has a twin on a model, with `mdl` in place of `env`, such as `BIYOS_setmdldblopt`. `BIYOS_delmdlopt` drops the model's value, so it reads the environment's again, and `BIYOS_getmdloptsrc` tells where the value it reads comes from:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/options.c" item="model_options"}
```

`threads` belongs to the environment alone, and every model call on it fails.

## Flags {#sec-options-flags}

A flags option switches the parts of an algorithm on or off. It holds two masks: the parts forced on and the parts forced off. A part in neither keeps its default.

## Versions {#sec-options-versions}

`BIYOS_getoptver` gives the versions that added, deprecated and retired an option:

```{.c file="examples/code/c/options.c" item="describe"}
```

A deprecated option still works, and setting it sends a warning naming the option to use instead. A retired option can be read but no longer set.

## Tolerances {#sec-options-tolerances}

`feastol_abs` and `feastol_rel` say when a value meets a bound or equals another value, `zerotol` when it is zero, and `inttol` when it is integral. With $\epsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}$ for `feastol_abs` and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}$ for `feastol_rel`, a value $v$ meets a lower bound $l$ unless

$$
l - v > \epsilon_{\mathrm{abs}} \quad\text{and}\quad l - v > \epsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} \cdot \max(1, |l|),
$$

and an upper bound alike. Two values $y$ and $z$ are equal unless they differ by more than both $\epsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}$ and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{rel}} \max(1, |y|, |z|)$. An infinite value or bound takes no tolerance, and NaN meets no bound and equals nothing.

Comparisons inside an expression, such as $e_1 \le e_2$ in a condition, follow the same rule with `cmptol_abs` and `cmptol_rel`. Both pairs default to $10^{-6}$, so a condition and a constraint on the same values agree. Setting both `cmptol` options to 0 makes comparisons exact.

## Time limits {#sec-options-limits}

`maxtime` limits the wall time of a solve and `maxcputime` its CPU time, both in seconds. The CPU time counted is that of the calling thread, so solves on other threads never spend each other's budget.

## Options in Python {#sec-options-python}

Python sets and reads options by name, with `setopt` and `getopt` on an environment or a model. The value's type must match the kind: an enum option takes a member of its class, such as `Checking.FULL`, and a flags option a `Masks(on, off)`. A mismatch raises `TypeError`.

```{.python file="examples/code/python/options.py"}
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Not used yet
biyos solves nothing yet, so options are only checked, stored and read back.
